title: Jimmy Rushing's change from ballads to blues
summary: Jones explains that Rushing sang ballads until Decca and New York turned him into a blues singer.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Was Miss Billie Holiday the first vocalist you had with the band?
Who had sung with you before that?
Jimmie and Billie were together then?

Of course. Jimmie was a balladeer. Jimmie only sang the blues for us once a night after the dance, but when we came to New York they changed the whole format with Decca since they had Andy Kirk and other peoples playing what they called the sweet tunes. So Jimmie started singing some blues so that made his vocal chords leave from what he was and most people didn't know and they forgot that Jimmie Rushing had been in New York in 1930. He came back in 1932; he sang ballads; he didn't sing no blues, but they made a blues singer out of him. He was converted; that was a conversion.
